data.title: AMIS maize 25 Nov: belt median eases 0.5% to Rs6,406 per 100 kg on eight mandis; Burewala slips to Rs6,125
data.summary: Belt median Rs6,406 per 100 kg (Rs2,563 per 40 kg) on 25 Nov versus Rs6,438 on 24 Nov, with Arifwala not reporting; Burewala fell to Rs6,125, Kamalia rose to Rs6,875 and Sahiwal stayed lowest at Rs4,650. Other Punjab mandis held at a Rs7,375 median on eight mandis (TT Singh Rs10,250, Lodhran Rs5,625).

data.title: Federal cabinet approves sugar deregulation: cane price left to the market, export subsidies and movement curbs end
data.summary: The cabinet approved the National Policy for Deregulation of the Sugar Sector on 24 Nov (Sindh cleared it on 21 Nov), ending government sugar and cane price controls, export subsidies and inter-provincial movement limits; more than 400,000 t of exports were approved on 20 Nov on top of about 200,000 t earlier. No crush start date or molasses measure was given, but removing price controls takes away a reason for mills to delay crushing.

data.title: CBOT 25 Nov settlements: Dec soybean meal $361.60 (+$8.60), Jan soybeans $12.44 (+10¢)
data.summary: Dec soybean meal settled $361.60/st on 25 Nov, up $8.60 (2.4%) from $353.00, and Jan meal $358.10; Jan soybeans closed 1,244¢ (+0.8%) and Dec soybean oil 58.08¢/lb, little changed. Rotterdam Feb–Apr soymeal offers rose €11 to €427/t FOB; US markets are shut on 26 Nov for Thanksgiving.

data.act: Keep buying dry new-crop in weekly lots, starting with Sahiwal (Rs46.5/kg for a fifth report, check moisture on such a low price), then Burewala (Rs61.3/kg), Pakpattan (Rs63.5/kg), Vehari (Rs63.8/kg) and Mailsi (Rs64.4/kg); Chichawatni is Rs65.0/kg, Kamalia Rs68.8/kg and Okara Rs74.8/kg. Reject lots above 14% moisture or failing aflatoxin.
data.why: The belt median was Rs64.1/kg on 25 Nov on eight mandis (Arifwala did not report), down 0.5% from Rs64.4/kg on 24 Nov; it is 4.9% above 25 Oct (Rs61.1/kg), 18.3% below a year ago (Rs78.4/kg on 25 Nov 2025) and at 34% of its 52-week range (Rs54.4–82.5/kg). Other Punjab mandis held at Rs73.8/kg, so the belt stays the cheapest source as autumn-crop arrivals peak in Nov–Dec.

data.act: Lock Dec–Jan needs this week with at least two crushers holding bean stocks before they reprice to a CBOT meal price now above $360/st; a licence lapse at end-November would tighten local supply further.
data.why: CBOT Dec soybean meal settled $361.60/st on 25 Nov, up $8.60 (2.4%) on the day and $15.90 since 23 Nov, with Jan at $358.10 and Jan soybeans at $12.44 after NOPA's low 46.6 lb/bu meal yield and fresh Chinese buying. Pakistan still buys meal from local crushers only: import approvals were deferred on 23 Oct and current GM soybean licences run only through November 2026, with no renewal found as of 26 Nov.

data.act: Hold 2–3 weeks of cover and top up only from existing stock; this week ask Okara-belt mills and two traders for fresh-crush start dates and quotes, and book the first lot when at least two nearby mills are crushing.
data.why: The federal cabinet approved sugar deregulation on 24 Nov, leaving cane prices to the market and ending export subsidies and movement curbs, after the ECC raised approved sugar exports to about 600,000 t (21 Nov); these were the millers' main reasons to hold back the Punjab crush, and the law requires a start by 30 Nov. Cane area is up 16% to 2.452 million acres, so fresh molasses should be ample once mills run.

data.note: Dec-26 settled $361.60 on 25 Nov, +$8.60 (2.4%), extending the NOPA-led rally; Jan-27 $358.10. Weekly change shown is for the week to 20 Nov. Dec expires 14 Dec; US closed 26 Nov.
Jan-27 closed 1,244¢ on 25 Nov, +10¢ (0.8%), with China buying 132,000 t of US beans. Weekly change shown is for the week to 20 Nov.
Dec-26 ended 58.08¢ on 25 Nov, marginally lower, holding near the nine-month low. Weekly change shown is for the week to 20 Nov.
